newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius Q1 profit up, but not comparative.
newsitem.headline: Danubius Q1 profit up, but not comparative.

text.p: The pre-tax profit of Hungarian hotel group Danubius rose to 600.3 million forints in the first quarter of 1997, but the figure is not fully cgmparative with a profit of 149.3 million forints in the same period of 1996, the company said on Thursday.
"The consolidated balance sheet and earnings report of Danubius Hotels Rt show substantial change due to the expansion gf the network," the company said in a statement.

The consolidated January-March figures of this year already included the hotel chain HungarHotels, which was acquired by the group last year, Danubius said, adding that the acquisition was followed by accounting changes at the companies.
Danubius did not disclose how much HungarHotels contributed to the consolidated profits.
The net sales of Danubius group rose to 3.076 billion forints in January-March from 2.811 billion forints in the same period of 1996, Danubius said.
The growth was 9.4 percent, while year-on-year consumer inflation ran at 18.8 percent in March.

The company added that Danubius Rt hotels accounted for 54.3 percent of the net sales in the first three months of this year, while the participation of HungarHotels was 37.7 percent. Another subsidiary, Helia Rt, contributed 7.3 percent.

The cash stock of the group decreased to 678 million forints in the first quarter of this year from 3.714 billion in the corresponding period of 1996, mainly due to payments following the acquisition of HungarHotels, Danubius said.
The credits taken up to finance the acquisition, and a 15 million German mark long-term loan of Helia, also boosted liabilities to 12.855 billion forints from 5.914 billion, Danubius said.
Danubius bought 85 percent of HungarHotels, which has 14 hotels, in September 1996 for 8.125 billion forints.
Danubius is 46.58 percent owned by foreign investors, while 34.38 percent of its shares is held by Hungary's INTERAG Rt and the remainder by Hungarian individuals and companies.
At 1008GMT, Danubius shares stood at 5,700 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange, unchanged from Wednesday.
